- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

109			Audience: jwt.ClaimStrings{audience},
110			IssuedAt: jwt.NewNumericDate(time.Now()),
111			Subject:  fmt.Sprint(userID),
112		}
113		if !expirationTime.IsZero() {
114			registeredClaims.ExpiresAt = jwt.NewNumericDate(expirationTime)
115		}
116	
117		// Declare the token with the HS256 algorithm used for signing, and the claims.
118		token := jwt.NewWithClaims(jwt.SigningMethodHS256, &ClaimsMessage{
119			Name:             username,
120			RegisteredClaims: registeredClaims,
121		})
122		token.Header["kid"] = KeyID
123	
124		// Create the JWT string.
125		tokenString, err := token.SignedString(secret)
126		if err != nil {
127			return "", err
128		}
129	
130		return tokenString, nil
131	}

133	// GenerateAccessTokenV2 generates a short-lived access token with user claims.
134	func GenerateAccessTokenV2(userID int32, username, role, status string, secret []byte) (string, time.Time, error) {
135		expiresAt := time.Now().Add(AccessTokenDuration)
136	
137		claims := &AccessTokenClaims{
138			Type:     "access",
139			Role:     role,
140			Status:   status,
141			Username: username,
142			RegisteredClaims: jwt.RegisteredClaims{
143				Issuer:    Issuer,
144				Audience:  jwt.ClaimStrings{AccessTokenAudienceName},
145				Subject:   fmt.Sprint(userID),
146				IssuedAt:  jwt.NewNumericDate(time.Now()),
147				ExpiresAt: jwt.NewNumericDate(expiresAt),
148			},
149		}
150	
151		token := jwt.NewWithClaims(jwt.SigningMethodHS256, claims)
152		token.Header["kid"] = KeyID
153	
154		tokenString, err := token.SignedString(secret)
155		if err != nil {
156			return "", time.Time{}, err
157		}
158	
159		return tokenString, expiresAt, nil
160	}

162	// GenerateRefreshToken generates a long-lived refresh token.
163	func GenerateRefreshToken(userID int32, tokenID string, secret []byte) (string, time.Time, error) {
164		expiresAt := time.Now().Add(RefreshTokenDuration)
165	
166		claims := &RefreshTokenClaims{
167			Type:    "refresh",
168			TokenID: tokenID,
169			RegisteredClaims: jwt.RegisteredClaims{
170				Issuer:    Issuer,
171				Audience:  jwt.ClaimStrings{RefreshTokenAudienceName},
172				Subject:   fmt.Sprint(userID),
173				IssuedAt:  jwt.NewNumericDate(time.Now()),
174				ExpiresAt: jwt.NewNumericDate(expiresAt),
175			},
176		}
177	
178		token := jwt.NewWithClaims(jwt.SigningMethodHS256, claims)
179		token.Header["kid"] = KeyID
180	
181		tokenString, err := token.SignedString(secret)
182		if err != nil {
183			return "", time.Time{}, err
184		}
185	
186		return tokenString, expiresAt, nil
187	}

189	// GeneratePersonalAccessToken generates a random PAT string.
190	func GeneratePersonalAccessToken() string {
191		randomStr, err := util.RandomString(32)
192		if err != nil {
193			// Fallback to UUID if RandomString fails
194			return PersonalAccessTokenPrefix + util.GenUUID()
195		}
196		return PersonalAccessTokenPrefix + randomStr
197	}

199	// HashPersonalAccessToken returns SHA-256 hash of a PAT.
200	func HashPersonalAccessToken(token string) string {
201		hash := sha256.Sum256([]byte(token))
202		return hex.EncodeToString(hash[:])
203	}

205	// verifyJWTKeyFunc returns a jwt.Keyfunc that validates the signing method and key ID.
206	func verifyJWTKeyFunc(secret []byte) jwt.Keyfunc {
207		return func(t *jwt.Token) (any, error) {
208			if t.Method.Alg() != jwt.SigningMethodHS256.Name {
209				return nil, errors.Errorf("unexpected signing method: %v", t.Header["alg"])
210			}
211			kid, ok := t.Header["kid"].(string)
212			if !ok || kid != KeyID {
213				return nil, errors.Errorf("unexpected kid: %v", t.Header["kid"])
214			}
215			return secret, nil
216		}
217	}

219	// ParseAccessTokenV2 parses and validates a short-lived access token.
220	func ParseAccessTokenV2(tokenString string, secret []byte) (*AccessTokenClaims, error) {
221		claims := &AccessTokenClaims{}
222		_, err := jwt.ParseWithClaims(tokenString, claims, verifyJWTKeyFunc(secret),
223			jwt.WithIssuer(Issuer),

228		}
229		if claims.Type != "access" {
230			return nil, errors.New("invalid token type: expected access token")
231		}
232		return claims, nil
233	}

244		}
245		if claims.Type != "refresh" {
246			return nil, errors.New("invalid token type: expected refresh token")
247		}

17	// Authenticator provides shared authentication and authorization logic.
18	// Used by gRPC interceptor, Connect interceptor, and file server to ensure
19	// consistent authentication behavior across all API endpoints.
20	//
21	// Authentication methods:
22	// - JWT access tokens: Short-lived tokens (15 minutes) for API access
23	// - Personal Access Tokens (PAT): Long-lived tokens for programmatic access
24	//
25	// This struct is safe for concurrent use.
26	type Authenticator struct {
27		store  *store.Store
28		secret string
29	}
30	
31	// NewAuthenticator creates a new Authenticator instance.
32	func NewAuthenticator(store *store.Store, secret string) *Authenticator {
33		return &Authenticator{
34			store:  store,
35			secret: secret,
36		}
37	}
38	
39	// AuthenticateByAccessTokenV2 validates a short-lived access token.
40	// Returns claims without database query (stateless validation).
41	func (a *Authenticator) AuthenticateByAccessTokenV2(accessToken string) (*UserClaims, error) {
42		claims, err := ParseAccessTokenV2(accessToken, []byte(a.secret))
43		if err != nil {
44			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid access token")
45		}
46	
47		userID, err := util.ConvertStringToInt32(claims.Subject)
48		if err != nil {
49			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid user ID in token")
50		}
51	
52		return &UserClaims{
53			UserID:   userID,
54			Username: claims.Username,
55			Role:     claims.Role,
56			Status:   claims.Status,
57		}, nil
58	}
59	
60	// AuthenticateByRefreshToken validates a refresh token against the database.
61	func (a *Authenticator) AuthenticateByRefreshToken(ctx context.Context, refreshToken string) (*store.User, string, error) {
62		claims, err := ParseRefreshToken(refreshToken, []byte(a.secret))
63		if err != nil {
64			return nil, "", errors.Wrap(err, "invalid refresh token")
65		}
66	
67		userID, err := util.ConvertStringToInt32(claims.Subject)
68		if err != nil {
69			return nil, "", errors.Wrap(err, "invalid user ID in token")
70		}
71	
72		// Check token exists in database (revocation check)
73		token, err := a.store.GetUserRefreshTokenByID(ctx, userID, claims.TokenID)
74		if err != nil {
75			return nil, "", errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get refresh token")
76		}
77		if token == nil {
78			return nil, "", errors.New("refresh token revoked")
79		}
80	
81		// Check token not expired
82		if token.ExpiresAt != nil && token.ExpiresAt.AsTime().Before(time.Now()) {
83			return nil, "", errors.New("refresh token expired")
84		}
85	
86		// Get user
87		user, err := a.store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{ID: &userID})
88		if err != nil {
89			return nil, "", errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get user")
90		}
91		if user == nil {
92			return nil, "", errors.New("user not found")
93		}
94		if user.RowStatus == store.Archived {
95			return nil, "", errors.New("user is archived")
96		}
97	
98		return user, claims.TokenID, nil
99	}

101	// AuthenticateByPAT validates a Personal Access Token.
102	func (a *Authenticator) AuthenticateByPAT(ctx context.Context, token string) (*store.User, *storepb.PersonalAccessTokensUserSetting_PersonalAccessToken, error) {
103		if !strings.HasPrefix(token, PersonalAccessTokenPrefix) {
104			return nil, nil, errors.New("invalid PAT format")
105		}
106	
107		tokenHash := HashPersonalAccessToken(token)
108		result, err := a.store.GetUserByPATHash(ctx, tokenHash)
109		if err != nil {
110			return nil, nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid PAT")
111		}
112	
113		// Check expiry
114		if result.PAT.ExpiresAt != nil && result.PAT.ExpiresAt.AsTime().Before(time.Now()) {
115			return nil, nil, errors.New("PAT expired")
116		}
117	
118		// Check user status
119		if result.User.RowStatus == store.Archived {
120			return nil, nil, errors.New("user is archived")
121		}
122	
123		return result.User, result.PAT, nil
124	}

126	// AuthResult contains the result of an authentication attempt.
127	type AuthResult struct {
128		User        *store.User // Set for PAT authentication
129		Claims      *UserClaims // Set for Access Token V2 (stateless)

133	// bearerAuth is the outcome of successfully validating a Bearer token: the resolved
134	// user plus the credential-specific detail needed to build an AuthResult.
135	type bearerAuth struct {
136		user   *store.User
137		claims *UserClaims                                                  // set for an Access Token V2
138		pat    *storepb.PersonalAccessTokensUserSetting_PersonalAccessToken // set for a Personal Access Token
139	}

141	// resolveBearer validates a Bearer token — an Access Token V2 or a Personal Access
142	// Token — into an active user. It returns:
143	//   - (nil, nil)    when the token is absent, malformed, expired, unknown, or resolves
144	//     to a missing/archived user (callers may then fall back to other credentials);
145	//   - (nil, err)    on an unexpected store error;
146	//   - (result, nil) on success.
147	//
148	// It performs no side effects; callers decide whether to record PAT usage.
149	func (a *Authenticator) resolveBearer(ctx context.Context, token string) (*bearerAuth, error) {
150		if token == "" {
151			return nil, nil
152		}
153	
154		if !strings.HasPrefix(token, PersonalAccessTokenPrefix) {
155			// Access Token V2 (stateless). An invalid token yields no identity and no
156			// error, so the caller can fall back to other credentials.
157			claims, err := a.AuthenticateByAccessTokenV2(token)
158			if err == nil && claims != nil {
159				user, err := a.store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{ID: &claims.UserID})
160				if err != nil {
161					return nil, err
162				}
163				if user != nil && user.RowStatus != store.Archived {
164					return &bearerAuth{user: user, claims: claims}, nil
165				}
166			}
167			return nil, nil
168		}
169	
170		// Personal Access Token.
171		if user, pat, err := a.AuthenticateByPAT(ctx, token); err == nil && user != nil {
172			return &bearerAuth{user: user, pat: pat}, nil
173		}
174		return nil, nil
175	}

177	// recordPATUsage updates a personal access token's last-used timestamp
178	// asynchronously; failures are logged and never affect the request.
179	func (a *Authenticator) recordPATUsage(userID int32, tokenID string) {
180		go func() {
181			if err := a.store.UpdatePATLastUsed(context.Background(), userID, tokenID, timestamppb.Now()); err != nil {
182				slog.Warn("failed to update PAT last used time", "error", err, "userID", userID)
183			}
184		}()
185	}

187	// AuthenticateToUser resolves the current request to a *store.User, checking the
188	// Authorization header first (access token or PAT), then falling back to the
189	// refresh token cookie. Returns (nil, nil) when no valid credentials are present.
190	func (a *Authenticator) AuthenticateToUser(ctx context.Context, authHeader, cookieHeader string) (*store.User, error) {
191		bearer, err := a.resolveBearer(ctx, ExtractBearerToken(authHeader))
192		if err != nil {
193			return nil, err
194		}
195		if bearer != nil {
196			return bearer.user, nil
197		}
198	
199		// Fallback: refresh token cookie.
200		if cookieHeader != "" {
201			if refreshToken := ExtractRefreshTokenFromCookie(cookieHeader); refreshToken != "" {
202				user, _, err := a.AuthenticateByRefreshToken(ctx, refreshToken)
203				return user, err
204			}
205		}
206	
207		return nil, nil
208	}
209	
210	// Authenticate resolves a Bearer token (Access Token V2 or PAT) into an AuthResult,
211	// returning nil when no valid credentials are present. Unlike AuthenticateToUser it
212	// ignores the refresh cookie, and it records PAT last-used on success.
213	func (a *Authenticator) Authenticate(ctx context.Context, authHeader string) *AuthResult {
214		token := ExtractBearerToken(authHeader)
215		bearer, err := a.resolveBearer(ctx, token)
216		if err != nil || bearer == nil {
217			return nil
218		}
219		if bearer.pat != nil {
220			a.recordPATUsage(bearer.user.ID, bearer.pat.TokenId)
221			return &AuthResult{User: bearer.user, AccessToken: token}
222		}
223		return &AuthResult{Claims: bearer.claims, AccessToken: token}
224	}

9	// ContextKey is the key type for context values.
10	// Using a custom type prevents collisions with other packages.
11	type ContextKey int
12	
13	const (
14		// UserIDContextKey stores the authenticated user's ID.
15		// Set for all authenticated requests.
16		// Use GetUserID(ctx) to retrieve this value.
17		UserIDContextKey ContextKey = iota
18	
19		// AccessTokenContextKey stores the JWT token for token-based auth.
20		// Only set when authenticated via Bearer token.
21		AccessTokenContextKey
22	
23		// UserClaimsContextKey stores the claims from access token.
24		UserClaimsContextKey
25	
26		// RefreshTokenIDContextKey stores the refresh token ID.
27		RefreshTokenIDContextKey
28	)

30	// GetUserID retrieves the authenticated user's ID from the context.
31	// Returns 0 if no user ID is set (unauthenticated request).
32	func GetUserID(ctx context.Context) int32 {
33		if v, ok := ctx.Value(UserIDContextKey).(int32); ok {
34			return v
35		}
36		return 0
37	}
38	
39	// GetAccessToken retrieves the JWT access token from the context.
40	// Returns empty string if not authenticated via bearer token.
41	func GetAccessToken(ctx context.Context) string {
42		if v, ok := ctx.Value(AccessTokenContextKey).(string); ok {
43			return v
44		}

17	// MetadataInterceptor converts Connect HTTP headers to gRPC metadata.
18	//
19	// This ensures service methods can use metadata.FromIncomingContext() to access
20	// headers like User-Agent, X-Forwarded-For, etc., regardless of whether the
21	// request came via Connect RPC or gRPC-Gateway.
22	type MetadataInterceptor struct{}
23	
24	// NewMetadataInterceptor creates a new metadata interceptor.
25	func NewMetadataInterceptor() *MetadataInterceptor {
26		return &MetadataInterceptor{}
27	}
28	
29	func (*MetadataInterceptor) WrapUnary(next connect.UnaryFunc) connect.UnaryFunc {
30		return func(ctx context.Context, req connect.AnyRequest) (connect.AnyResponse, error) {
31			// Convert HTTP headers to gRPC metadata
32			header := req.Header()
33			md := metadata.MD{}
34	
35			// Copy important headers for client info extraction
36			if ua := header.Get("User-Agent"); ua != "" {
37				md.Set("user-agent", ua)
38			}
39			if origin := header.Get("Origin"); origin != "" {
40				md.Set("origin", origin)
41			}
42			if xff := header.Get("X-Forwarded-For"); xff != "" {
43				md.Set("x-forwarded-for", xff)
44			}
45			if xfp := header.Get("X-Forwarded-Proto"); xfp != "" {
46				md.Set("x-forwarded-proto", xfp)
47			}
48			if xri := header.Get("X-Real-Ip"); xri != "" {
49				md.Set("x-real-ip", xri)
50			}
51			if forwarded := header.Get("Forwarded"); forwarded != "" {
52				md.Set("forwarded", forwarded)
53			}
54			// Forward Cookie header for authentication methods that need it (e.g., RefreshToken)
55			if cookie := header.Get("Cookie"); cookie != "" {
56				md.Set("cookie", cookie)
57			}
58	
59			// Set metadata in context so services can use metadata.FromIncomingContext()
60			ctx = metadata.NewIncomingContext(ctx, md)
61	
62			// Execute the request
63			resp, err := next(ctx, req)
64	
65			// Prevent browser caching of API responses to avoid stale data issues
66			// See: https://github.com/usememos/memos/issues/5470
67			if !isNilAnyResponse(resp) && resp.Header() != nil {
68				resp.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate")
69				resp.Header().Set("Pragma", "no-cache")
70				resp.Header().Set("Expires", "0")

72	
73			return resp, err
74		}

93	// LoggingInterceptor logs Connect RPC requests with appropriate log levels.
94	//
95	// Log levels:
96	// - INFO: Successful requests and expected client errors (not found, permission denied, etc.)
97	// - ERROR: Server errors (internal, unavailable, etc.)
98	type LoggingInterceptor struct {
99		logStacktrace bool
100	}

102	// NewLoggingInterceptor creates a new logging interceptor.
103	func NewLoggingInterceptor(logStacktrace bool) *LoggingInterceptor {
104		return &LoggingInterceptor{logStacktrace: logStacktrace}

108		return func(ctx context.Context, req connect.AnyRequest) (connect.AnyResponse, error) {
109			resp, err := next(ctx, req)
110			in.log(req.Spec().Procedure, err)
111			return resp, err

123	func (in *LoggingInterceptor) log(procedure string, err error) {
124		level, msg := in.classifyError(err)
125		attrs := []slog.Attr{slog.String("method", procedure)}
126		if err != nil {
127			attrs = append(attrs, slog.String("error", err.Error()))
128			if in.logStacktrace {
129				attrs = append(attrs, slog.String("stacktrace", fmt.Sprintf("%+v", err)))
130			}
131		}
132		slog.LogAttrs(context.Background(), level, msg, attrs...)
133	}

135	func (*LoggingInterceptor) classifyError(err error) (slog.Level, string) {
136		if err == nil {
137			return slog.LevelInfo, "OK"
138		}
139	
140		var connectErr *connect.Error
141		if !pkgerrors.As(err, &connectErr) {
142			return slog.LevelError, "unknown error"
143		}
144	
145		// Client errors (expected, log at INFO)
146		switch connectErr.Code() {
147		case connect.CodeCanceled,
148			connect.CodeInvalidArgument,
149			connect.CodeNotFound,
150			connect.CodeAlreadyExists,
151			connect.CodePermissionDenied,
152			connect.CodeUnauthenticated,
153			connect.CodeResourceExhausted,
154			connect.CodeFailedPrecondition,
155			connect.CodeAborted,
156			connect.CodeOutOfRange:
157			return slog.LevelInfo, "client error"
158		default:
159			// Server errors
160			return slog.LevelError, "server error"
161		}
162	}

205	// AuthInterceptor enforces authentication and anonymous-access policy for Connect

12	// ErrUnauthenticated is returned by the Authorizer when a request must be rejected
13	// for lack of valid credentials. Each transport maps it to its own status code
14	// (Connect: CodeUnauthenticated, gRPC-Gateway: HTTP 401).
15	var ErrUnauthenticated = errors.New("authentication required")
16	
17	// Authorizer is the single source of truth for method-level access control.
18	//
19	// It authenticates a request from its Authorization header and decides whether the
20	// (possibly anonymous) caller may reach a given RPC procedure. The Connect
21	// interceptor and the gRPC-Gateway middleware share one Authorizer so both
22	// transports enforce identical rules.
23	//
24	// Role-based authorization (admin checks) stays in the service layer; this type
25	// governs only authentication and anonymous access.
26	type Authorizer struct {
27		authenticator *auth.Authenticator
28		store         *store.Store
29		profile       *profile.Profile
30	}
31	
32	// NewAuthorizer creates an Authorizer backed by the given store, token secret, and
33	// instance profile.
34	func NewAuthorizer(store *store.Store, secret string, profile *profile.Profile) *Authorizer {
35		return &Authorizer{
36			authenticator: auth.NewAuthenticator(store, secret),
37			store:         store,
38			profile:       profile,
39		}
40	}

42	// Authenticate resolves the caller from the Authorization header, returning nil for
43	// an anonymous request. It never enforces policy — pair it with CheckAccess.
44	func (a *Authorizer) Authenticate(ctx context.Context, authHeader string) *auth.AuthResult {
45		return a.authenticator.Authenticate(ctx, authHeader)
46	}
47	
48	// CheckAccess enforces method-level access policy for procedure given the
49	// authentication result (nil = anonymous). It returns nil when the request is
50	// permitted and ErrUnauthenticated otherwise.
51	//
52	// Policy:
53	//   - Authenticated caller (access token or PAT): always permitted here.
54	//   - Anonymous + protected method: denied.
55	//   - Anonymous + public method, open instance: permitted.
56	//   - Anonymous + public method, private instance (no InstanceURL): permitted only
57	//     for the auth-bootstrap set, plus CreateUser during first-run setup.
58	func (a *Authorizer) CheckAccess(ctx context.Context, procedure string, result *auth.AuthResult) error {
59		if result != nil {
60			return nil
61		}
62		if !IsPublicMethod(procedure) {

55	// ClaimsMessage represents the claims structure in a JWT token.
56	//
57	// JWT Claims include:
58	// - name: Username (custom claim)
59	// - iss: Issuer = "memos"
60	// - aud: Audience = "user.access-token"
61	// - sub: Subject = user ID
62	// - iat: Issued at time
63	// - exp: Expiration time (optional, may be empty for never-expiring tokens).
64	type ClaimsMessage struct {
65		Name string `json:"name"` // Username
66		jwt.RegisteredClaims
67	}

69	// AccessTokenClaims contains claims for short-lived access tokens.
70	// These tokens are validated by signature only (stateless).
71	type AccessTokenClaims struct {
72		Type     string `json:"type"`     // "access"
73		Role     string `json:"role"`     // User role
74		Status   string `json:"status"`   // User status

87	// GenerateAccessToken generates a JWT access token for a user.
88	//
89	// Parameters:
90	// - username: The user's username (stored in "name" claim)
91	// - userID: The user's ID (stored in "sub" claim)
92	// - expirationTime: When the token expires (pass zero time for no expiration)
93	// - secret: Server secret used to sign the token
94	//
95	// Returns a signed JWT string or an error.
96	func GenerateAccessToken(username string, userID int32, expirationTime time.Time, secret []byte) (string, error) {
97		return generateToken(username, userID, AccessTokenAudienceName, expirationTime, secret)
98	}
99	
100	// generateToken generates a JWT token with the given claims.
101	//
102	// Token structure:
103	// Header: {"alg": "HS256", "kid": "v1", "typ": "JWT"}
104	// Claims: {"name": username, "iss": "memos", "aud": [audience], "sub": userID, "iat": now, "exp": expiry}
105	// Signature: HMACSHA256(base64UrlEncode(header) + "." + base64UrlEncode(payload), secret).
106	func generateToken(username string, userID int32, audience string, expirationTime time.Time, secret []byte) (string, error) {
107		registeredClaims := jwt.RegisteredClaims{
108			Issuer:   Issuer,
109			Audience: jwt.ClaimStrings{audience},
110			IssuedAt: jwt.NewNumericDate(time.Now()),
111			Subject:  fmt.Sprint(userID),
112		}
113		if !expirationTime.IsZero() {
114			registeredClaims.ExpiresAt = jwt.NewNumericDate(expirationTime)
115		}
116	
117		// Declare the token with the HS256 algorithm used for signing, and the claims.
118		token := jwt.NewWithClaims(jwt.SigningMethodHS256, &ClaimsMessage{
119			Name:             username,
120			RegisteredClaims: registeredClaims,
121		})
122		token.Header["kid"] = KeyID
123	
124		// Create the JWT string.
125		tokenString, err := token.SignedString(secret)
126		if err != nil {
127			return "", err
128		}
129	
130		return tokenString, nil
131	}

133	// GenerateAccessTokenV2 generates a short-lived access token with user claims.
134	func GenerateAccessTokenV2(userID int32, username, role, status string, secret []byte) (string, time.Time, error) {
135		expiresAt := time.Now().Add(AccessTokenDuration)
136	
137		claims := &AccessTokenClaims{
138			Type:     "access",
139			Role:     role,
140			Status:   status,
141			Username: username,
142			RegisteredClaims: jwt.RegisteredClaims{
143				Issuer:    Issuer,
144				Audience:  jwt.ClaimStrings{AccessTokenAudienceName},
145				Subject:   fmt.Sprint(userID),
146				IssuedAt:  jwt.NewNumericDate(time.Now()),
147				ExpiresAt: jwt.NewNumericDate(expiresAt),
148			},
149		}
150	
151		token := jwt.NewWithClaims(jwt.SigningMethodHS256, claims)
152		token.Header["kid"] = KeyID
153	
154		tokenString, err := token.SignedString(secret)
155		if err != nil {
156			return "", time.Time{}, err
157		}
158	
159		return tokenString, expiresAt, nil
160	}

162	// GenerateRefreshToken generates a long-lived refresh token.
163	func GenerateRefreshToken(userID int32, tokenID string, secret []byte) (string, time.Time, error) {
164		expiresAt := time.Now().Add(RefreshTokenDuration)
165	
166		claims := &RefreshTokenClaims{
167			Type:    "refresh",
168			TokenID: tokenID,
169			RegisteredClaims: jwt.RegisteredClaims{
170				Issuer:    Issuer,
171				Audience:  jwt.ClaimStrings{RefreshTokenAudienceName},
172				Subject:   fmt.Sprint(userID),
173				IssuedAt:  jwt.NewNumericDate(time.Now()),
174				ExpiresAt: jwt.NewNumericDate(expiresAt),
175			},
176		}
177	
178		token := jwt.NewWithClaims(jwt.SigningMethodHS256, claims)
179		token.Header["kid"] = KeyID
180	
181		tokenString, err := token.SignedString(secret)
182		if err != nil {
183			return "", time.Time{}, err
184		}
185	
186		return tokenString, expiresAt, nil
187	}

189	// GeneratePersonalAccessToken generates a random PAT string.
190	func GeneratePersonalAccessToken() string {
191		randomStr, err := util.RandomString(32)
192		if err != nil {
193			// Fallback to UUID if RandomString fails
194			return PersonalAccessTokenPrefix + util.GenUUID()
195		}
196		return PersonalAccessTokenPrefix + randomStr

199	// HashPersonalAccessToken returns SHA-256 hash of a PAT.
200	func HashPersonalAccessToken(token string) string {
201		hash := sha256.Sum256([]byte(token))
202		return hex.EncodeToString(hash[:])
203	}

205	// verifyJWTKeyFunc returns a jwt.Keyfunc that validates the signing method and key ID.
206	func verifyJWTKeyFunc(secret []byte) jwt.Keyfunc {
207		return func(t *jwt.Token) (any, error) {
208			if t.Method.Alg() != jwt.SigningMethodHS256.Name {
209				return nil, errors.Errorf("unexpected signing method: %v", t.Header["alg"])
210			}
211			kid, ok := t.Header["kid"].(string)
212			if !ok || kid != KeyID {
213				return nil, errors.Errorf("unexpected kid: %v", t.Header["kid"])
214			}
215			return secret, nil
216		}
217	}

219	// ParseAccessTokenV2 parses and validates a short-lived access token.
220	func ParseAccessTokenV2(tokenString string, secret []byte) (*AccessTokenClaims, error) {
221		claims := &AccessTokenClaims{}

231		}
232		return claims, nil

244		}
245		if claims.Type != "refresh" {
246			return nil, errors.New("invalid token type: expected refresh token")
247		}

17	// Authenticator provides shared authentication and authorization logic.
18	// Used by gRPC interceptor, Connect interceptor, and file server to ensure
19	// consistent authentication behavior across all API endpoints.
20	//
21	// Authentication methods:
22	// - JWT access tokens: Short-lived tokens (15 minutes) for API access
23	// - Personal Access Tokens (PAT): Long-lived tokens for programmatic access
24	//
25	// This struct is safe for concurrent use.
26	type Authenticator struct {
27		store  *store.Store
28		secret string
29	}
30	
31	// NewAuthenticator creates a new Authenticator instance.
32	func NewAuthenticator(store *store.Store, secret string) *Authenticator {
33		return &Authenticator{
34			store:  store,
35			secret: secret,
36		}
37	}
38	
39	// AuthenticateByAccessTokenV2 validates a short-lived access token.
40	// Returns claims without database query (stateless validation).
41	func (a *Authenticator) AuthenticateByAccessTokenV2(accessToken string) (*UserClaims, error) {
42		claims, err := ParseAccessTokenV2(accessToken, []byte(a.secret))
43		if err != nil {
44			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid access token")
45		}
46	
47		userID, err := util.ConvertStringToInt32(claims.Subject)
48		if err != nil {
49			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid user ID in token")
50		}
51	
52		return &UserClaims{
53			UserID:   userID,
54			Username: claims.Username,
55			Role:     claims.Role,
56			Status:   claims.Status,
57		}, nil
58	}
59	
60	// AuthenticateByRefreshToken validates a refresh token against the database.
61	func (a *Authenticator) AuthenticateByRefreshToken(ctx context.Context, refreshToken string) (*store.User, string, error) {
62		claims, err := ParseRefreshToken(refreshToken, []byte(a.secret))
63		if err != nil {
64			return nil, "", errors.Wrap(err, "invalid refresh token")
65		}
66	
67		userID, err := util.ConvertStringToInt32(claims.Subject)
68		if err != nil {
69			return nil, "", errors.Wrap(err, "invalid user ID in token")
70		}
71	
72		// Check token exists in database (revocation check)
73		token, err := a.store.GetUserRefreshTokenByID(ctx, userID, claims.TokenID)
74		if err != nil {
75			return nil, "", errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get refresh token")
76		}
77		if token == nil {
78			return nil, "", errors.New("refresh token revoked")
79		}
80	
81		// Check token not expired
82		if token.ExpiresAt != nil && token.ExpiresAt.AsTime().Before(time.Now()) {
83			return nil, "", errors.New("refresh token expired")
84		}
85	
86		// Get user
87		user, err := a.store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{ID: &userID})
88		if err != nil {
89			return nil, "", errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get user")
90		}
91		if user == nil {
92			return nil, "", errors.New("user not found")
93		}
94		if user.RowStatus == store.Archived {
95			return nil, "", errors.New("user is archived")
96		}
97	
98		return user, claims.TokenID, nil
99	}
100	
101	// AuthenticateByPAT validates a Personal Access Token.
102	func (a *Authenticator) AuthenticateByPAT(ctx context.Context, token string) (*store.User, *storepb.PersonalAccessTokensUserSetting_PersonalAccessToken, error) {
103		if !strings.HasPrefix(token, PersonalAccessTokenPrefix) {
104			return nil, nil, errors.New("invalid PAT format")
105		}
106	
107		tokenHash := HashPersonalAccessToken(token)
108		result, err := a.store.GetUserByPATHash(ctx, tokenHash)
109		if err != nil {
110			return nil, nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid PAT")
111		}
112	
113		// Check expiry
114		if result.PAT.ExpiresAt != nil && result.PAT.ExpiresAt.AsTime().Before(time.Now()) {
115			return nil, nil, errors.New("PAT expired")
116		}
117	
118		// Check user status
119		if result.User.RowStatus == store.Archived {
120			return nil, nil, errors.New("user is archived")
121		}
122	
123		return result.User, result.PAT, nil
124	}
125	
126	// AuthResult contains the result of an authentication attempt.
127	type AuthResult struct {
128		User        *store.User // Set for PAT authentication
129		Claims      *UserClaims // Set for Access Token V2 (stateless)
130		AccessToken string      // Non-empty if authenticated via JWT
131	}
132	
133	// bearerAuth is the outcome of successfully validating a Bearer token: the resolved
134	// user plus the credential-specific detail needed to build an AuthResult.
135	type bearerAuth struct {
136		user   *store.User
137		claims *UserClaims                                                  // set for an Access Token V2
138		pat    *storepb.PersonalAccessTokensUserSetting_PersonalAccessToken // set for a Personal Access Token
139	}
140	
141	// resolveBearer validates a Bearer token — an Access Token V2 or a Personal Access
142	// Token — into an active user. It returns:
143	//   - (nil, nil)    when the token is absent, malformed, expired, unknown, or resolves
144	//     to a missing/archived user (callers may then fall back to other credentials);
145	//   - (nil, err)    on an unexpected store error;
146	//   - (result, nil) on success.
147	//
148	// It performs no side effects; callers decide whether to record PAT usage.
149	func (a *Authenticator) resolveBearer(ctx context.Context, token string) (*bearerAuth, error) {
150		if token == "" {
151			return nil, nil
152		}
153	
154		if !strings.HasPrefix(token, PersonalAccessTokenPrefix) {
155			// Access Token V2 (stateless). An invalid token yields no identity and no
156			// error, so the caller can fall back to other credentials.
157			claims, err := a.AuthenticateByAccessTokenV2(token)
158			if err == nil && claims != nil {
159				user, err := a.store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{ID: &claims.UserID})
160				if err != nil {
161					return nil, err
162				}
163				if user != nil && user.RowStatus != store.Archived {
164					return &bearerAuth{user: user, claims: claims}, nil
165				}
166			}
167			return nil, nil
168		}
169	
170		// Personal Access Token.
171		if user, pat, err := a.AuthenticateByPAT(ctx, token); err == nil && user != nil {
172			return &bearerAuth{user: user, pat: pat}, nil
173		}
174		return nil, nil
175	}
176	
177	// recordPATUsage updates a personal access token's last-used timestamp
178	// asynchronously; failures are logged and never affect the request.
179	func (a *Authenticator) recordPATUsage(userID int32, tokenID string) {
180		go func() {
181			if err := a.store.UpdatePATLastUsed(context.Background(), userID, tokenID, timestamppb.Now()); err != nil {
182				slog.Warn("failed to update PAT last used time", "error", err, "userID", userID)
183			}
184		}()
185	}
186	
187	// AuthenticateToUser resolves the current request to a *store.User, checking the
188	// Authorization header first (access token or PAT), then falling back to the
189	// refresh token cookie. Returns (nil, nil) when no valid credentials are present.
190	func (a *Authenticator) AuthenticateToUser(ctx context.Context, authHeader, cookieHeader string) (*store.User, error) {
191		bearer, err := a.resolveBearer(ctx, ExtractBearerToken(authHeader))
192		if err != nil {
193			return nil, err
194		}
195		if bearer != nil {
196			return bearer.user, nil
197		}
198	
199		// Fallback: refresh token cookie.
200		if cookieHeader != "" {
